explanation: Ammonia in stale urine helps lift grease and dirt from wool. Fullers collected it from pots in the streets, and the emperor Vespasian taxed its collection.

claims.text: Roman fullers, who cleaned and finished cloth, used urine to clean clothes, as at Pompeii before AD 79.
Ammonia from stale urine helps remove grease and dirt from wool.
Urine for the fulleries was collected from containers in public places.
The emperor Vespasian imposed a tax on the collection of urine.
